sections.html:
Expect to deal with Hardin County offices. Taxes come from the sheriff, deeds are recorded by the clerk, and code or permit questions go to city hall. First, though, choose how to sell: list with an agent, line up a buyer yourself, or take an as-is cash offer. The three differ in speed and in who pays for repairs.

The city is the Hardin County seat and ranked ninth in Kentucky in the 2020 count. Its metro area spans Hardin, Meade and Larue counties and takes in Radcliff, Vine Grove, Rineyville and the housing areas of Fort Knox, which lies about 15 miles north.

Population was 31,394 in 2020 and is estimated at 35,448 for July 1, 2025, up 12.9%. Just 49.3% of homes are lived in by their owners, which makes rentals a big slice of the market. Typical house value runs $245,900, with gross rent at $909 and household income at $60,760. The 2020 count found 13,095 households in 14,076 housing units, with 7.0% of units vacant.

Interstate 65 passes through town, roughly 30 miles south of Louisville and 80 miles from Bowling Green. The Western Kentucky Parkway begins at the I-65 interchange, and the Bluegrass Parkway heads about 105 miles east to Lexington. Elizabethtown Regional Airport (EKX) handles local flying. Commutes average 20 minutes, and the job base leans toward manufacturing and health care. Summers are humid, so buyers will probably check air conditioning and crawl-space moisture.

Hardin County bills the person who owned the house on January 1, even if it sells later that year. Pay the sheriff by mail or at 150 North Provident Way, Suite 101. Paying online or by card adds a 2.49% fee. Call 270-765-5133 and press option 1.

Hardin County sheriff: bill by payment period
Payment periodWhat you owe
NovemberBill less the discount
DecemberFace amount
JanuaryFace amount plus 5%
February 1 through April 15Face amount plus 21%

Splitting the bill is not an option: the sheriff takes no partial payments on the current year and no prorated shares from seller and buyer. Someone pays it all, and the closing statement evens things out. Tax districts 03 (Radcliff) and 06 (Vine Grove) carry separate city tax payment details on the sheriff's site. For an older unpaid year, ring the Hardin County Clerk at 270-765-2171 and ask for a payoff.

People aged 65 or over, and people who are totally disabled, apply to the Hardin County PVA (270-765-2129) for this reduction. It lowers the assessed value by $49,100 in the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. Since it follows the person and not the house, a buyer must file a new claim after closing.

sections.h2: Transfer tax and other closing costs
sections.html:
KRS 142.050 charges the seller $0.50 for each $500 block of value stated in the deed, rounding any remainder up to a whole block. The clerk collects before accepting the deed. Exempt deeds include foreclosure deeds, deeds between spouses and nominal-price deeds from parent to child.

On top of that come your mortgage payoff, your share of the year's tax and any concessions the buyer wins after inspection. Agent fees apply only when you list with one.

sections.h2: Which school district is a house in?
sections.html: Two systems cover the city. Elizabethtown Independent Schools operates its own campuses, while Hardin County Schools serves a portion of the city limits, Central Hardin High School among them. A few schools use an Elizabethtown mailing address yet sit in Radcliff, and Central Hardin uses a Cecilia address. Check the district and tax district printed on your bill before you tell a buyer where a house is zoned.

City Code Enforcement covers property maintenance, zoning compliance, nuisance violations and unsafe conditions. Call and find out if your address has an open file. If you added a room or deck years ago, Planning and Development can tell you whether permits were pulled.

An inherited house takes more prep. Title has to pass to the heirs, or the estate's representative has to sign the deed, so talk to the county clerk and a Kentucky attorney before listing.

Get these done before the first offer and closing moves faster.

  • Find your latest Hardin County bill and check the name printed on it.
  • Learn from the clerk whether any earlier year is unpaid, and get the figure in writing.
  • Order a mortgage payoff letter dated near the closing day you expect.
  • Ask Code Enforcement and Planning about open files or permits that were never closed out.
  • Settle in the contract who fixes what, or sell the house as it stands.

Keep copies of everything you sign, including the deed and the settlement statement. If a question about taxes or title comes up months later, the county offices will ask for those papers, and having them in one folder saves you a trip to the courthouse.

Cash buyers need no lender sign-off, so deferred repairs or an unpaid tax bill rarely stall them. What you owe is subtracted from the sale money when you sign.

A cash offer for the house as it stands drops most of the steps that drag out a regular listing. No appraiser can undercut the price, no mortgage approval can collapse, and no punch list arrives after the inspection. You skip staging, open houses and the weeks spent waiting on someone else's loan.

County paperwork does not go away. The deed still gets recorded, transfer tax still applies, and any lien or unpaid tax must be settled before title is clear. Ask a cash buyer for the final amount you would walk away with, then compare it with a listing's likely result after fees and repairs.

A title company or an attorney's office in Hardin County usually hosts the signing. You sign the deed, the agent uses your proceeds to clear the mortgage and any open tax, and transfer tax reaches the clerk with the recorded deed. Take a photo ID and your keys, and ask in advance to see the settlement statement line by line.

Selling for an estate, or a house still titled to a relative? Have the court or legal papers ready early, because nobody closes until it is clear who may sign. Moving out of town? Leave the sheriff a forwarding address. The next bill goes to whoever is on record, and a missed notice means penalties for somebody.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Hardin County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Send it to the sheriff's office at 150 North Provident Way, Suite 101, or bring it in. Cards cost an extra 2.49%, and the office can issue a duplicate if nothing arrived by early November.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax does an Elizabethtown seller pay?
faqs.a: Fifty cents for every $500 block of value on the deed, with any partial block rounded up. It is due from the seller and paid to the clerk at recording.

faqs.q: Who owes the tax when an Elizabethtown house sells mid year?
faqs.a: Whoever owned it January 1 is on the bill. The closing agent splits the year between you and the buyer, but a single party hands the sheriff the full amount.

faqs.q: Is Elizabethtown in the Elizabethtown or Hardin County school district?
faqs.a: Both serve parts of the city. The district printed on your bill settles the question.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Elizabethtown house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes, some buyers will take one with open violations. Find out from Code Enforcement what is on file so your contract names who fixes each item.
